title: CJP activists detained during Panaji protest demand EC resignation

tea.why: Activists protested against alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls.
tea.want: They demanded the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
tea.changed: Oct 11: The Bombay High Court ordered the immediate release of detained activists during a special night sitting.

summary: Activists affiliated with the Cockroach Janta Party staged a demonstration at Azad Maidan in Panaji, Goa, to demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and protest against alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls. The district administration had previously denied permission for the gathering. Police detained several protesters, including hotelier Jack Sukhija and other activists, after they breached a security cordon and waved the national flag, moving them to the Pernem Police Station. Following an urgent habeas corpus petition, the Bombay High Court's Goa bench held a special Sunday evening hearing and ordered the immediate release of the detained individuals after receiving an undertaking that they would not return to protest at Azad Maidan that night. Despite the initial police action and restrictions, hundreds of supporters gathered near the locked gates and continued demonstrations at the Panjim Municipal Garden.
demands: Resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar
response: According to the police, protesters were detained because they proceeded with a public gathering after the North Goa Collector rejected their application for permission. (Sources: 1, 2)

arrests.text: Seven protesters were detained by the police

updates.text: Goa Police detained several protesters at Azad Maidan in Panaji ahead of a planned demonstration.
The Bombay High Court held a special evening sitting and ordered the immediate release of detained protesters.
